10 Wisconsin Labor Day Weekend Events Worth a Road Trip: September 4–7, 2026

September 5, 2026September 5, 2026
ShareShare
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:10
Instaread

Labor Day weekend may represent summer’s unofficial finale, but Wisconsin isn’t exactly going quietly.

Access Online Encyclopedias

You can toss dried cow manure for distance in Prairie du Sac, watch kilted athletes hurl heavy objects in Waukesha, eat your way around the State Capitol in Madison, celebrate 175 years of the Sheboygan County Fair, explore nearly 200 artists in Milwaukee or encounter everything from classic cars to cheese along Kenosha’s lakefront.

Head north and Door County adds art, marina festivities and a brand-new jazz celebration, while Black River Falls offers an opportunity to experience one of Wisconsin’s important Native American cultural traditions.

Here are 10 Wisconsin festivals and events worth building a Labor Day weekend road trip around, September 4–7, 2026.

1. Taste of Madison — Madison

Discover more
Rent Event Decor
Travel
Submit Award Entries

September 5–6
Where: Capitol Square
Road trip routes: I-39/90/94, U.S. 12/18 & U.S. 151

Come hungry! Taste of Madison surrounds the Wisconsin State Capitol with more than 90 food vendors, beverage stands and two live music stages. Admission is completely free; you simply purchase whatever food and drinks tempt you along the way.

Consult Labor Attorneys

Saturday runs from 2–9 p.m., with Sunday continuing from 11 a.m.–7 p.m. The event has been a Labor Day weekend tradition since 1983, and participating volunteer organizations help generate more than $90,000 annually for local nonprofits.

The location doesn’t hurt, either. Few Wisconsin food festivals come with a backdrop quite like Capitol Square.

Taste of Madison official site

2. Wisconsin State Cow Chip Throw & Festival — Prairie du Sac

Discover more
Music
Download Travel Guides
PODCAST

September 4–5
Road trip routes: U.S. 12, Highways 60 & 78

Some states throw cabers. Wisconsin throws cow manure.

Book Vacation Rentals

The legendary Wisconsin State Cow Chip Throw & Festival returns to Prairie du Sac with competitors seeing just how far they can propel a dried cow chip. The serious throwing takes place Saturday, but there’s plenty happening around it.

Saturday includes a 5K and 10K, an arts and crafts fair with more than 125 exhibitors, children’s activities, live entertainment and the wonderfully named Tournament of Chips Parade at noon.

The event is quirky, unmistakably Wisconsin and close enough to Baraboo, Devil’s Lake and the Wisconsin River to build a considerably larger road trip around it.

Wisconsin State Cow Chip Throw schedule

3. Wisconsin Highland Games — Waukesha

September 4–6
Where: Waukesha County Expo Center
Road trip routes: I-94, Highways 59 & 164

Bagpipes, Highland dancing and very strong people wearing kilts take over Waukesha this weekend.

Try Time Trackers

The Wisconsin Highland Games celebrate Scottish, Irish and Celtic heritage with pipe-and-drum competitions, cultural demonstrations, parades, workshops, Celtic music and traditional heavy athletics.

Friday’s opening celebration runs 5–10 p.m., followed by full days Saturday and Sunday. Watch competitors tackle traditional strength events, explore the clan tents or settle into the pub tent for live music.

And yes, the caber toss involves attempting to flip what essentially looks like a telephone pole. Don’t try that at home.

Wisconsin Highland Games official site

4. Third Ward Art Festival — Milwaukee

September 5–6
Where: Historic Third Ward
Road trip routes: I-43, I-794 & Highway 32

Milwaukee’s Historic Third Ward becomes a giant outdoor gallery over Labor Day weekend.

Book Walking Tours

Nearly 200 juried artists from around the country display paintings, photography, ceramics, glass, jewelry, fiber art, mixed media and more along Broadway. Artists offer demonstrations and booth chats, while live music, children’s art activities and food add to the street-festival atmosphere. Admission is free, and the Third Ward provides plenty of restaurants, shops, galleries and Milwaukee River scenery when you’re ready for a break from browsing.

Historic Third Ward Labor Day weekend information

5. Kenosha Classic Cruise-In & Cheese-A-Palooza — Kenosha

September 5
Where: Downtown and Kenosha Harbor
Road trip routes: I-94, Highways 32, 50 & 158

Reserve Expo Passes

Here’s a nice two-for-one road trip.

The 23rd Kenosha Classic Cruise-In expects more than 1,500 classic cars, trucks and motorcycles to fill downtown Kenosha from 9 a.m.–4 p.m. Saturday. Admission is free both for spectators and for displaying a vehicle.

Then wander a few blocks toward the harbor for Cheese-A-Palooza, featuring food, cold beverages and free music from 11 a.m.–11 p.m.

Lake Michigan, classic cars, Wisconsin cheese and live music? That’s a fairly efficient use of a Saturday.

Kenosha Classic Cruise-In details from Visit Kenosha

6. Ho-Chunk Nation Labor Day Pow-Wow — Black River Falls

September 5–7
Road trip routes: I-94, Highways 27 & 54

The Ho-Chunk Nation Pow-Wow offers visitors an opportunity to experience an important Wisconsin cultural tradition over Labor Day weekend.

Access Online Encyclopedias

The Ho-Chunk Nation welcomes friends and neighbors to this gathering of thanksgiving, with traditional drumming and dancing accompanied by the vivid colors and intricate designs of dancers’ regalia. Vendors from around the country also offer crafts and other items.

The Pow-Wow is free and open to the public, with free parking.

For travelers interested in Wisconsin history and Native American culture, this is one of the weekend’s most meaningful destinations.

Ho-Chunk Nation Pow-Wow information from Travel Wisconsin

7. Door County Labor Day Weekend — Sister Bay, Gills Rock & Sturgeon Bay

Discover more
Order Demographic Reports
Stream New Podcasts
Podcast

September 5–6
Road trip routes: Highways 42 & 57

Door County gives you several events to string together into one road trip this weekend.

Consult Labor Attorneys

Marina Fest fills the Sister Bay waterfront Saturday and Sunday with live music, food, beverages and children’s activities. Continue north on Highway 42 and you’ll reach the 24th annual Gills Rock Art Fest, featuring professional artists, jewelry, three-dimensional works, food and afternoon music from 9 a.m.–4 p.m. both days.

Then Sturgeon Bay launches Jazz on Jefferson. A Saturday evening kickoff leads into Sunday’s main event from noon–8 p.m., with live jazz, artisan vendors, food and beverages along Jefferson Street, followed by a late-night open jam.

That’s enough activity to justify simply pointing the car north and making a weekend of Highway 42.

Destination Door County Labor Day event listing

8. Rock River Thresheree — Edgerton

September 4–7
Road trip routes: I-39/90, U.S. 51, Highways 26 & 59

If you enjoyed Door County’s Valmy Thresheree a few weeks ago, here’s another chance to watch Wisconsin’s mechanical past come back to life.

Discover Local Events

The Rock River Thresheree features operating antique steam engines, tractors and machinery along with a working sawmill, pile driver, blacksmith shop, antique cars and trucks and military displays.

You can ride the Rock River Cannonball train, browse a large flea market, watch equipment demonstrations and catch the daily Parade of Power at 2 p.m.

The show runs 8 a.m.–5 p.m. all four days.

Rock River Thresheree information from Travel Wisconsin

9. Sheboygan County Fair — Plymouth

September 3–7
Road trip routes: Highways 23, 57 & 67

Book Vacation Rentals

The Sheboygan County Fair celebrates its 175th anniversary this Labor Day weekend, and organizers are marking the milestone with five days of carnival rides, animals, agricultural exhibits, fair food, music and grandstand entertainment.

Saturday brings rising country star Chase Matthew with Hayden Coffman to the grandstand at 7 p.m. Then Sunday adds something decidedly more 21st-century to the 175-year-old fair: a drone light show.

The fair runs through Labor Day Monday at the Sheboygan County Fairgrounds in Plymouth, a few miles south of Highway 23 and close to both Elkhart Lake and the Kettle Moraine.

Calculate Shipping Costs

Sheboygan County Fair official site

10. Prentice Progress Days — Prentice

September 4–7
Road trip routes: U.S. 8, Highway 13

For a Northwoods Labor Day road trip, Prentice Progress Days packs an impressive amount into a village of fewer than 700 people.

Try Time Trackers

Friday brings a street dance and the Northwoods Truck Show’s Semi Glow & Show. Saturday adds a parade, craft vendors, softball, free children’s rides and live music including country artist Hailey James and Pink Houses. Sunday includes an auto show, fishing contest and more activities before the weekend concludes Monday.

Admission to the celebration is free.

Prentice also sits along Highway 13 in Price County, making Progress Days a good destination for exploring the forests and lakes of north-central Wisconsin.

Prentice Progress Days details from Travel Wisconsin

Pick Some Roads and GO!

Labor Day weekend is one of those times when almost every direction offers something interesting.

Head south for classic cars in Kenosha. Go west for Ho-Chunk culture or cow-chip throwing. Follow Highway 42 north through Door County. Eat your way around Madison’s Capitol Square. Listen for bagpipes in Waukesha. Or celebrate a remarkable 175 years of county-fair tradition in Plymouth.

And remember: Labor Day may be the unofficial end of summer, but it’s certainly not the end of Wisconsin road-trip season.

Fall festivals—and eventually those spectacular Wisconsin colors—are right around the corner.
